overall_summary: Analysis of FACTVERSE performance data shows that high-concept space and astrophysics scenarios—particularly extreme 'What If' planetary explorations and unique planetary phenomena—generate the highest views-per-day and engagement (likes/comments per view). Specifically, videos centered around bizarre planetary environments (e.g., liquid diamond planets, burning ice, extreme weather) outperform standard abstract facts or general psychological tricks by a wide margin.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) garnered over 1,000 and 972 views rapidly with strong like-to-view ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on immersive, second-person hypothetical space survival scenarios involving extreme alien worlds.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing impossible-sounding space truths like 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (QXuqYERlqSo) pulled massive relative traction compared to standard historical or basic science facts.
winning_patterns.action: Use high-contrast cosmic anomalies as hook foundations, pairing counter-intuitive physics with vivid, high-stakes visual imagery.

weak_patterns.pattern: Abstract Psychological Trivia Without High Stakes
weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (2fqaGqfsR4A, r43-7nSn8SQ) and general memory/song-stuck facts consistently underperformed, pulling single-digit to low double-digit views.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standalone psychological tips unless tied to a high-urgency, cinematic mystery narrative or micro-story.

weak_patterns.evidence: Vague historical mysteries like 'The 2,000-Year-Old Mystery Science Can't Solve' (yLm-FjYH6-k) show sluggish daily views compared to aggressive space content.
weak_patterns.action: Shift historical storytelling toward high-tension micro-mysteries or country-specific dark legends rather than broad ancient trivia.
